content.title: 2026 World Baseball Classic: Venezuela top USA to win resounding first championship
content.text: USA skipper Mark DeRosa: "Not going to make excuses" Venezuela deservedly beat a star-studded U.S. team on this night behind excellent pitching, starting with Eduardo Rodríguez who gave them 4-1/3 scoreless innings. The Venezuelans suffocated USA throughout the game, allowing just three hits, two of them by Bryce Harper — including a game-tying two-run home run in the bottom of the eighth. The U.S. had not even advanced a runner past first through the opening seven innings. Venezuela struck first in the third when García drove home Pérez with a one-out sac fly. Wilyer Abreu compounded the damage in the fifth with his second homer of this Classic to make it a 2-0 game. Harper came to the hosts’ rescue in the eighth with his dramatic round-tripper to even the score. But in the next inning, Venezuela pulled away again, Eugenio Suárez doubling in what would be the decisive run before closer Palencia slammed the door on a triumphant win. Venezuela dismissed defending champions Japan in the quarter-finals and tournament darlings Italy in the semis en route to the final. And they convinced the world in doing it, with some excellent baseball along the way. Venezuela will have all of Wednesday to celebrate it, which has been decreed a national holiday. “When Harper hit the homer, everyone was kind of down,” Pérez said of Harper’s electric blast over the center field wall. “But they only tied the game. We’re still in the game, I was like, come on guys, let’s go. It’s only 2-2 - it’s like 0-0. That’s what I told my team-mates.” Added García, “I’m proud to be a part of this group and I’m proud to be representing 30 million Venezuelans back in my country. “The next time you guys do a ranking of baseball, Venezuela is No. 1.” USA manager Mark DeRosa did not cut any excuses for the defeat, tipping his hat to his opposite number. “I’m not going to make excuses,” DeRosa said. “It’s early in spring training, guys are getting ready for the season. Eventually the tournament gets moved and the guys are in better form pitching-wise. “For whatever reason, we just couldn’t get it rolling offensively. Even tonight, you look up in the seventh and they had a two-hit shutout. “Hats off to them. For them to battle last night against Italy, for them to use their entire bullpen, those guys to come back out on no rest was pretty special to watch.”
